findings.finding: Step 3 justifies that the absolute-path-launched jira-capability-probe.py will resolve rebar.reconciler.* after engine_env stops prepending PYTHONPATH by claiming the probe 'already imported rebar.*' — but the probe's actual imports are `rebar_reconciler.access_check` and `rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.acli`, which the codemod rewrites to `rebar.reconciler.*`. The real precondition (rebar is pip-installed in sys.executable's site-packages so a submodule resolves without PYTHONPATH) is asserted but not pinned by any AC; the `-m rebar.reconciler` fresh-venv AC covers the module-launch path but not the absolute-path probe launch.
scenarios: A deployment where `rebar` is on PATH but not importable from the launching interpreter's site-packages (e.g. pipx shim, PATH-only rebar) runs `rebar bridge check-access`; the probe subprocess with no PYTHONPATH fails at `import rebar.reconciler.access_check`.
findings.suggested_fix: State the actual precondition: `rebar` must be installed (importable) in the interpreter that launches the probe, since engine_env no longer prepends the package dir. Add an AC that runs `src/rebar/_engine/jira-capability-probe.py` via `[sys.executable, script]` with PYTHONPATH unset and asserts it imports rebar.reconciler.access_check / .adapters.jira.acli (credentials-missing exit 2 is acceptable as an import-success signal).
